newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Rain dampens Australian sorghum trade - Grainco.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rain dampens Australian sorghum trade - Grainco.

text.p: An already-quiet domestic sorghum market was not helped last week by unfavourable weather in southern Queensland, Grainco trading manager Rob Brealey said in its weekly market review.
With the possibility of further feed grains stocks because of quality downgrading of wheat and barley, many consumers remained on the sideline waiting for a clearer picture, he said.

Because of the rain there was only limited trade in the domestic sorghum market over the past week, with both old and new crop bids remaining around the A$115.00 a tonne and A$120.00 a tonne rerspectively, delivered port.
Domestic feed barley values were steady last week in response to the unfavourable weather. The export market was also quiet.
Export values for malting barley remained well-supported as international buyers, particularly China, looked to Australia for anticipated production levels.
Strong overseas demand for Australian malting barley had a stabilising effect on the local market.
Buyers continued to show concern over the large price differential of US$50-$60 between export feed and malt barley.
Domestically, malt barley values were firmer over the past week.
The cottonseed market was not active and from an export perspective Japanese importers were slowly coming to terms with tightening old crop Australian supply, Brealey said.
Domestic business remained at a low ebb.
In pulses, with the southern harvest approaching and delivered port trade escalating, pulse markets were coming under more pressure, he said.
Faba bean prices dropped away as domestic trade opens up.
Middle Eastern consumers have adequate coverage through into the new year.
Chickpea prices stabilised over the last weak or so.
Domestic oilseed values were slightly lower than the previous week.
